papers.title: Polar Geometry of Time-Odd EEG Dynamics
papers.summary: The paper introduces a skew-symmetric EEG state-derivative operator K and its spectral counterpart to extract time-odd, subject-discriminative longitudinal EEG features. Across four public datasets, polar orientation improved cross-session subject matching (e.g., Dortmund AUC 0.8901→0.9625, CMC@1 0.4757→0.6214), with fixed alpha-beta fusion reaching CMC@1=0.8350 and AUC=0.9855.

papers.title: Comparison of the Utility of Amplitude-Spectral and Coherence Features of Psychotropic Drugs' Action on ECoG Signal for Pharmaco-EEG Based Drug Screening in Rats.
papers.summary: Compared naive Bayesian classification of pharmaco-EEG data using amplitude-spectral features, coherence features, and their combination to identify psychoactive drug mechanisms in rats. Combined features correctly classified 20 of 24 test drug groups, while amplitude-spectral or coherence alone each classified 18 of 24; adding coherence significantly improved accuracy (p < 0.01).

papers.title: REM sleep suppression after penetrating traumatic brain injury is associated with alterations in the supramammillary-hippocampal circuit.
papers.summary: In a rat model of penetrating traumatic brain injury (pTBI), severe focal pTBI produced sustained suppression of REM sleep and REM-associated theta oscillations, associated with decreased Vglut2 within the supramammillary-hippocampal circuit and reduced orexin A and melanin-concentrating hormone in the lateral hypothalamus.

papers.title: Mu or alpha? Source decomposition for social perception analysis.
papers.summary: Compared sensor-level EEG with ICA-based source separation to assess whether central mu rhythm during emotional face perception is contaminated by visual alpha. ICA revealed distinct mu and alpha sources with opposite dynamics; mu showed synchronization and minimal sensitivity to facial expressions, suggesting prior mu suppression findings may reflect alpha contamination.

papers.title: Img2EEG: A Scalable and Interpretable Encoding Framework for Simulating Human EEG Responses to Visual Inputs.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The paper introduces Img2EEG, a participant-specific image-to-EEG encoding framework integrating hierarchical visual and semantic representations to generate temporally resolved EEG responses. Trained on THINGS EEG2, it generalized to unseen images, reproduced the face-sensitive N170, and scaled to 1.28 million ImageNet images producing over 12 million synthetic EEG responses that supported cross-dataset visual reconstruction.

papers.title: A hierarchical graph learning framework for VR-based motor imagery decoding driven by MVMD and feature optimization.
papers.summary: This study proposes a hierarchical graph learning framework for VR-based motor imagery decoding, using multivariate variational mode decomposition, hybrid feature selection, and a hierarchical graph convolutional network on phase locking value brain networks. On a lab-acquired VR-MI dataset, the framework achieved competitive three-class decoding accuracy surpassing EEGNet and revealed VR-induced modulations in brain network organization.

papers.title: Not all N3 sleep is equal: EEG-defined N3 sleep depth and health-related quality of life in the sleep heart health study.
papers.summary: In 5469 Sleep Heart Health Study participants, EEG-defined N3 sleep depth (odds ratio product during N3) was independently associated with lower physical and mental health-related quality of life, while N3 duration showed no significant linear association. Longitudinally, higher baseline ORPN3 was associated with lower follow-up physical component summary.

papers.title: Cross-variability decoding for motor imagery EEG signals: a comprehensive review.
papers.summary: This review provides a comprehensive taxonomy of cross-variability decoding methods for motor imagery EEG from 2020 to 2025. It critically evaluates deep learning and transfer learning approaches, including CNNs, transformers, feature alignment, domain adaptation, and meta-learning, across cross-subject and cross-session variability paradigms.

papers.title: NPD-RSVP: A novel BCI paradigm and decoding method for target recognition.
papers.summary: The study proposes a negative photographic dual-RSVP (NPD) paradigm and a cross-frequency decoupling model (CFDM) for EEG decoding in a brain-computer interface. On an expanded dataset of 20 subjects, the method achieved mean classification accuracy of 94.24% and true positive rate of 90.62% for target recognition.

papers.title: Inter-rater reliability on rhythmic and periodic EEG patterns using Standardized Computer-based Organized Reporting of EEG (SCORE): A multicenter study.
papers.summary: Multicenter study assessed inter-rater reliability of rhythmic and periodic EEG patterns, background activity, and interictal findings using the SCORE framework across 10 EpiCARE centers. Overall RPP identification reached substantial agreement (κML .61–.66), individual RPP types almost perfect (κML up to .98), while posterior dominant rhythm reliability was low (κML .06–.47).

papers.title: Frequency-Specific EEG burst dynamics in Parkinson's Disease and freezing of gait.
papers.summary: In resting-state EEG from 237 participants, people with Parkinson's disease showed more frequent but shorter low-beta bursts at mid-frontal regions compared to healthy controls, while theta burst amplitude metrics were most consistently associated with freezing of gait severity.

papers.title: Implications of Wearable Sleep Health Technology for Cardiovascular Health Assessment and Interventions: A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on wearable sleep health technologies for cardiovascular assessment, finding that these devices consistently show high sensitivity but lower specificity for detecting wake compared to polysomnography, with some consumer devices performing comparably to research-grade actigraphy and headband EEG systems approaching polysomnography-level staging.

papers.title: Electroencephalographic changes during hyperbaric oxygen therapy in patients with chronic disorders of consciousness.
papers.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: In 40 patients with prolonged disorders of consciousness undergoing hyperbaric oxygen therapy, permutation entropy and Lempel-Ziv complexity increased progressively across sessions in all brain regions, paralleling improvements in Coma Recovery Scale-Revised scores, while power spectral density remained largely stable.

papers.title: MERIT: A No-Code Platform for Unifying High-Precision Cognitive Assessment Across Laboratory and Real-World Settings.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: By injecting stimulus-timing jitter into an EEG dataset, this study found that the N170 component tolerated up to 15.8 ms jitter under a prespecified criterion, while MMN and P3 tolerated more than 20 ms; the authors then developed MERIT, a no-code platform achieving inter-stimulus-interval SDs of 0.71–0.96 ms on current mobile devices, well below these thresholds.

papers.title: Reassessing Global Field Synchronization as a Phase-Synchrony EEG Metric: Mathematical Review and Empirical Counterexamples With Implications for Wearable Pain Monitoring.
papers.summary: Evaluated whether global field synchronization (GFS) validly represents EEG phase synchronization using synthetic simulations and empirical resting-state EEG. Simulations showed GFS was invariant to rotations that changed circular standard deviation and varied with scaling, while empirical data lacked a consistent inverse relationship between GFS and CSD across frequency bands, indicating GFS is not a valid proxy for phase synchronization.

papers.title: From normative values to pain assessment models: A large-scale study of laser-evoked brain responses.
papers.summary: Using EEG from 936 participants, this study established normative values for laser-evoked potentials and developed a predictive model showing that N1, N2, and P2 amplitudes, N2 latency, and gamma-band event-related synchronization mediate the relationship between stimulus intensity and subjective pain perception.

papers.title: Acute administration of methylphenidate modulates functional connectivity during irrelevant stimuli processing in Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled cross-over trial examined acute methylphenidate (20 mg) effects on event-related EEG functional connectivity in Parkinson's disease patients during a visual oddball task. Compared to placebo, methylphenidate decreased theta-band functional connectivity and global efficiency in fronto-parietal networks during processing of task-irrelevant standard stimuli.

papers.title: EXPRESS: NEUROPROTECTIVE EFFICACY OF AN OMEGA-3 DIGLYCERIDE EMULSION IN A PIGLET MODEL OF NEWBORN HYPOXIC-ISCHEMIC BRAIN DAMAGE.
papers.journal: Journal of cerebral blood flow and metabolism : official journal of the International Society of Cerebral Blood Flow and Metabolism
papers.summary: In a piglet model of newborn hypoxic-ischemic brain damage, acute treatment with omega-3 diglyceride emulsion after hypoxia-ischemia partially restored early EEG recovery, attenuated cell death and neuroinflammatory markers, and limited protein carbonyl formation and GFAP+ cell loss, with efficacy preserved under hypothermia. The emulsion was well tolerated with no hemodynamic or respiratory side effects.

papers.title: Voice and linguistic features support early attentional filtering of irrelevant stimuli.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: In an EEG study of auditory attention, listeners attended to lateralized target syllables while distractor streams were manipulated for voice and linguistic content. Both acoustic (voice) and linguistic dissimilarity of distractors independently improved early attentional filtering, as reflected by larger target-evoked EEG responses, and recall was poor only when both voice and linguistic content were similar.

papers.title: Multi-modal connectome analysis of the stereoelectroencephalography implantation effect: a case report.
papers.summary: In a single case of drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy, longitudinal multimodal connectome analysis showed that SEEG implantation was associated with decreased hippocampus-amygdala and fusiform-temporal pole connectivity, increased hippocampus-posterior cingulate connectivity, and reduced connectome gradient eccentricity (11.9% after SEEG, 17.6% after lobectomy), alongside lymphocytic infiltration and reactive gliosis around electrode trajectories.

papers.title: Quantum machine learning for detection of sleep deprivation from EEG signals
papers.summary: This study applied Quantum Support Vector Machine and Hybrid Quantum Neural Networks to classify sleep-deprived versus well-rested states using resting-state EEG features, including spectral band power, band ratios, Hjorth parameters, and functional connectivity. The Hybrid Quantum Neural Network achieved the highest performance with 96.88% accuracy at the epoch level and 81.25% at the subject level, outperforming previously reported results.

papers.title: Clinical Implementation of Amplitude-Integrated Electroencephalography for Neonatal Seizure Detection and Prognostication: First National Experience From North Macedonia.
papers.summary: A prospective observational study of 64 neonates in North Macedonia evaluated amplitude-integrated EEG (aEEG) for seizure detection and prognostication. Electrographic seizures were significantly more frequent in neonates with clinically suspected seizures than in high-risk neonates without clinical events (51.5% vs 25.8%), and abnormal aEEG background was the strongest predictor of adverse neurodevelopmental outcome (OR 9.62).

papers.title: Cue validity moderates the effects of haptic feedback in simulated instrument flight.
papers.summary: This study examined whether haptic cue validity moderates pilot situational awareness and performance in simulated instrument flight, with eye-tracking and EEG. Haptic cueing improved altitude adherence and increased altimeter fixation, while control participants had better heading adherence and showed higher workload and fatigue and lower engagement on EEG.

papers.title: Clinical and preclinical investigation of the mechanism promoting aura in post-traumatic headache and inhibition of pain-related behavior in mice by onabotulinumtoxinA.
papers.summary: In humans, 32% of patients with post-traumatic headache developed new-onset aura, and in a mouse model of mTBI, injured mice showed a 160% increase in cortical spreading depression (CSD) induction probability; onabotulinumtoxinA did not alter CSD susceptibility but completely abolished optogenetic CSD-induced allodynia.

papers.title: Neural Responsivity to Unexpected Stimuli Moderates a Developmental Pathway to Anxiety: A Community-Sample Replication in Early Infancy and Childhood.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: In 147 infants from a community sample, the mismatch response (MMR) at 4 months moderated developmental pathways from negative reactivity to behavioral inhibition and from behavioral inhibition to childhood anxiety. More negative MMR was associated with risk pathways, and anxiety symptoms were stable from 30 months to 4–6 years.

papers.title: Aging of lexical selection and phonological encoding in Chinese spoken word production: An EEG study.
papers.summary: Using a picture-word interference paradigm with EEG, this study found that older adults showed larger word and syllable frequency effects but reduced phonological facilitation compared to younger adults, with ERP decoding revealing later and less temporally stable representations of syllable frequency and phonological facilitation in older adults.

papers.title: Understanding the impact of perceived emotional valence of eco-labels for novel food products on consumer preferences, visual attention, and cognition - a multimodal study using EEG and eye tracking.
papers.summary: This multimodal EEG and eye-tracking study found that eco-labels with high perceived positivity increased purchase intentions, were associated with shorter fixation durations and fewer fixations, and modulated P300 and LPP amplitudes; higher P300 increased purchase intentions while greater N200 reduced them for high-positivity labels.

papers.title: Case Report: Seizure freedom after resection of a temporal choroidal fissure cyst in drug-resistant epilepsy.
papers.summary: A 35-year-old woman with drug-resistant epilepsy and a right temporal choroidal fissure cyst achieved seizure freedom (Engel Class IA/ILAE Class 1) after SEEG-guided radiofrequency thermocoagulation followed by anterior temporal lobectomy; SEEG and intraoperative ECoG confirmed an epileptogenic focus adjacent to the cyst, with no histopathological evidence of hippocampal sclerosis or focal cortical dysplasia.

papers.title: Neural Dynamics of Self-Control: Pre-Choice EEG Signals Predict Yielding to Temptation
papers.summary: Introduced a dynamometer-based task in which 26 participants chose between high-effort/larger-later and low-effort/smaller-sooner rewards during 32-channel EEG, producing frequent switching toward smaller-sooner options in temptation trials. Pre-choice late positive potential differentiated stay from switch trials, and multivariate decoding discriminated outcomes 304–348 ms post-option presentation via frontal and centroparietal networks, indicating that neural bias toward yielding is established before the initial choice and reflects reward anticipation rather than self-control signals.

papers.title: Bilateral Angular Gyrus 810-nm Transcranial Near-Infrared Stimulation Reshapes Brain Network: Ameliorate Alzheimer's Disease Cognitive Deficits.
papers.summary: In a randomized, sham-controlled trial of 36 biomarker-confirmed Alzheimer's disease patients, targeted 810-nm transcranial near-infrared stimulation over the bilateral angular gyrus improved cognition, memory, language, attention, and executive functions while reducing neuropsychiatric symptoms. fMRI showed enhanced default mode network connectivity and functional synergy with dorsal attention, frontoparietal, and limbic networks, and TMS-EEG demonstrated enhanced information flow and prefrontal/temporo-occipital activation.

papers.title: PFKFB2 Gates a Relationship Between Cardiac Glycolytic Regulation and Electrophysiological Function.
papers.summary: Cardiomyocyte-specific PFKFB2 knockout mice exhibited prolonged QT and action potential duration, impaired Ca2+ reuptake, increased spontaneous Ca2+ release via O-GlcNAcylation, and ventricular tachyarrhythmia that was enhanced in the fed state, indicating that glycolytic dysregulation at the phosphofructokinase nexus promotes electrophysiological instability.

papers.title: A rare de novo contiguous 15q11.1-q13.3 duplication with tetrasomy (CN=4) and adjacent trisomy (CN=3) associated with severe global developmental delay, autism spectrum disorder, and subclinical epileptiform discharges: a case report and literature review.
papers.summary: This case report describes a Chinese girl with a de novo contiguous 15q11.1-q13.3 duplication comprising a ~10.34 Mb tetrasomic segment and an adjacent ~2.40 Mb trisomic segment, presenting with severe global developmental delay, autism spectrum disorder, profound cognitive and language impairment, delayed myelination, and subclinical epileptiform discharges. The findings expand the genomic spectrum of complex proximal 15q rearrangements and highlight the value of high-resolution genomic testing.

papers.title: Hirschsprung's disease and a rare mutation of the PIGO gene: Mabry syndrome.
papers.summary: Case report of a 2-year-old Turkish boy with Mabry syndrome (HPMRS2) due to a novel homozygous PIGO p.Arg445Pro variant, presenting with neurodevelopmental delay, seizures, hyperphosphatasia, and Hirschsprung's disease. Rectal biopsy confirmed aganglionosis; after definitive surgery, spontaneous defecation was achieved except for rare enterocolitis episodes.

papers.title: Hemimegalencephaly with accelerated myelination in the affected hemisphere.
papers.summary: Case report of a 7-month-old boy with left hemimegalencephaly presenting with neonatal-onset seizures and developmental delay. Brain MRI showed hemispheric enlargement, dysmorphic gyri, an aberrant midsagittal fiber tract, and accelerated myelination in the affected hemisphere, illustrating a recognizable imaging pattern for early diagnosis.

papers.title: Aphasic Status Epilepticus as a Stroke Mimic: A Literature Review.
papers.summary: A literature review of 87 reported cases of aphasic status epilepticus found that global aphasia was most common, treatment was delayed more than one week in 32% of attacks, and aphasia sequelae occurred in 20% of attacks, emphasizing that aphasic status epilepticus should be considered a stroke mimic requiring immediate benzodiazepine treatment.

papers.title: Synergistic effects of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation and a dance movement intervention on mild cognitive impairment: study protocol for a four-arm factorial randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a four-arm factorial randomized controlled trial to evaluate the synergistic effects of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) and a culturally tailored dance movement intervention on cognitive function in older adults with mild cognitive impairment, with the primary outcome being global cognition measured by the Montreal Cognitive Assessment.

papers.title: Top developments in clinical cardiac electrophysiology-2025.
papers.summary: No abstract is available for this review article titled 'Top developments in clinical cardiac electrophysiology-2025'.

papers.title: Electrophysiology procedures for preventing falls in older people living in the community.
papers.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
papers.summary: This is a protocol for a Cochrane systematic review that will assess the efficacy and safety of electrophysiology procedures in preventing falls among older people living in the community. No results are reported.

papers.title: Foster care intervention protects cognitive control skills in young adults exposed to institutional rearing.
papers.summary: In the Bucharest Early Intervention Project 22-year follow-up, young adults randomized to foster care showed event-related potential markers of performance monitoring comparable to never-institutionalized controls, whereas those who remained in institutional care exhibited disrupted cognitive control associated with lower IQ and elevated mental health symptoms.

papers.title: Eye-Tracking Research: A Bibliometric Analysis Based on Scopus.
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis of 45,230 Scopus-indexed eye-tracking publications found substantial growth during 2020-2025, with 22,130 publications in that period. The study maps productive authors, institutions, countries, and thematic trends, showing increased prominence of EEG, virtual reality, augmented reality, computer vision, machine learning, and deep learning.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
